findings.problem: The reader trusts a historical snapshot without detecting newer committed history beyond revision + 1. Restoring an older feature.json can therefore conceal a committed scope_change and expose its revoked approval as active. The approved D4 algorithm assumes the one-revision invariant instead of checking it against manual edits.
findings.failure_scenario: Create and claim a run, then register a calibrated plan and spec/ac/design bindings (revision 6). Commit approve_plan ap-1 (revision 7), then scope_change s-1 (revision 8). Restore only feature.json to its saved revision-6 bytes, leaving all history intact. Confirmed using production load and next handlers with in-memory file reads: next returns exit 0, revision 7, action dispatch, approval ap-1; committed history/8.json still contains the revocation. No forged digest or modified history is needed.
findings.basis: AC-D02 requires direct state-file edits to be detected on the next read and never treated as approval. DUR-01 requires controller-only state changes. D4 itself warns that restoring older state can revive revoked approvals. Existing manual-edit tests cover changed fields, but not restoration of a valid historical snapshot.
findings.expected_fix: Revise D4 and the regression plan to detect inconsistent or rolled-back current state before returning an older revision. Return untrusted_state with a concrete reason and file list, preserving files. Add tests for this approval/revocation sequence, legitimate one-revision crash recovery, and concurrent reads/writes so detection does not reject valid concurrent progress.

scope: Reviewed the complete product change, acceptance tests, planning artifacts, applicable decisions/high-level design, CI/packaging and commit text at the requested head. No additional blocking scope or commit-convention issue found. Production contains no dispatch execution, GitHub reads, G1/G3 evaluation, test-only hooks or temporary stubs. CI structure matches D12 and validation §6.1, including SHA pins and verified PR-head checkout. No files were modified.
limits: Full pytest, lint, mypy and distribution checks were not rerun under the strict read-only constraint; coordinator-reported G1 results remain supplied evidence. G2-01 was reproduced with Python 3.12 using production reader/CLI code and in-memory file reads, not physical filesystem mutation. Historical Red evidence was not checked. GitHub API connectivity failed, so actual PR checks, artifacts and action-SHA resolution were not verified. The G22 acceptance demonstration and physical power-loss durability were not verified.
